title: Ruben Loftus-Cheek to undergo surgery on fractured teeth and jaw
content:
AC Milan and England midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek will undergo surgery after fracturing his teeth and jaw.

Loftus-Cheek, 30, was taken off on a stretcher with his head in a brace following a collision during Milan’s defeat to Parma on Sunday.

Milan confirmed in a club statement he would undergo surgery on Monday after suffering fractures to his upper teeth and maxillary alveolar bone — part of the jaw which contains the tooth sockets.

The club added that tests had shown the midfielder had avoided a concussion and not lost consciousness.

Loftus-Cheek suffered the injury following a collision with Parma goalkeeper Edoardo Corvi as the pair contested an aerial ball. A number of Parma players immediately gestured for play to be stopped and for Loftus-Cheek and Corvi to receive medical attention.

The England international was pictured with a bloodied face as he was taken off the pitch on a stretcher in the 11th minute and was replaced by Ardon Jashari.

Loftus-Cheek has made 27 appearances in all competitions this season, scoring three goals and providing one assist.

In September, he received his first England call up in six years and appeared as a substitute during October’s win over Wales. It marked his first England appearance since November 2018. He was not included in the subsequent November squad as Thomas Tuchel’s side concluded their World Cup qualifying campaign ahead of this summer’s tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

Milan are second in Serie A and return to action against Cremonese on Sunday.
